Body: I'd like to take a crack at this. The fix is minimal - in `resolvePromptParts()` in `packages/opencode/src/session/prompt.ts`, the template text part can be marked `synthetic: true`: ```typescript const parts: PromptInput["parts"] = [ { type: "text", text: template, synthetic: true, }, ] ``` The `synthetic` flag already has the right semantics - it's used throughout the codebase to mark content that's sent to the model but hidden from the user (file reads, bookkeeping messages, etc.). The filtering is already in place everywhere parts are rendered, so no UI changes are needed in either the TUI or the web/desktop app. I've validated this locally in OpenWork as well and it hides the command=>skill prompt parts as desired. Optionally, a companion `ignored: true` part could show a short confirmation like "Running skill: skill-name" so the user gets visual feedback without seeing the full template. I've validated this locally in OpenWork as well - as an example -> Happy to open a PR if this approach works for you. cc @thdxr

## Senior Code Review Summary
Reviewing PR #1598 "Add unified adoption application mode" at commit 5f0be46e (fix: resolve PR reviews for #1598). This PR implements a tenant-level adoption application mode allowing rescues to choose between species-specific forms or a unified adoption form.

### 🔴 Critical, High & Security Issues
No critical or security issues identified. The implementation appears sound with proper validation and error handling.

### 🟡 Medium Priority & Logic Gaps
- [ ] **[Medium]** Potential N+1 query in website config health check (apps/api/src/http/websiteRoutes.ts:115-130)
  - *Proposed Fix:* Consider combining the prisma.websiteConfig.findFirst and applicationTemplateActive.findFirst queries into a single transaction or using select clauses more efficiently to reduce database round trips.

- [ ] **[Medium]** Inconsistent error handling in tenantRoutes.ts PUT handler (apps/api/src/http/tenantRoutes.ts:390-405)
  - *Proposed Fix:* The error response for invalid adoptionApplicationMode returns 400 but doesn't match the exact format of other validation errors in the codebase. Consider standardizing error response format.

### 🟢 Refactoring & DRY Opportunities
- [ ] **[Refactoring]** Duplicate scope validation logic between applicationTemplatesRoutes.ts and websiteRoutes.ts
  - *Suggestion:* Extract the unified scope validation into a shared utility function to avoid duplication.

- [ ] **[Refactoring]** Hardcoded 'All' string in multiple places
  - *Suggestion:* Use the UNIFIED_ADOPTION_SCOPE_KEY constant consistently instead of hardcoding 'All' in websiteRoutes.ts health check.

- [ ] **[Refactoring]** Redundant null coalescing in tenantRoutes.ts
  - *Suggestion:* The line `adoptionApplicationMode: cfg?.adoptionApplicationMode ?? 'species-specific',` could be simplified since the database column has a default value.

The PR is ready for merge with minor improvements recommended. The implementation correctly addresses the requirements in issue #1592 and maintains backward compatibility.

> These are not agent avatars, these are projects. Are you suggesting that the app should show the indicator on top of the project avatar, whenever at least one session is working?

Yes, that is absolutely correct. I have many projects running sessions in parallel. I would like to be able to see an indicator on the projects that have active running sessions. I think currently, it only shows an indicator when there is a session that has finished. Sometimes, I have a long running (45min+) run going and I completely forget that it's running because there is no visual indicator. So, I forget to check in on it and make sure that it is still heading in the right direction. Or even worse, I think that all my sessions are done and I shut down my laptop and head home for the day. I come in the next day only to realize that there was an active session that I killed the day before because I didn't know that it was still running.

Sorry for being persistent, but I invested more time testing this against a real monorepo/multi-repo workflow to see if per-session directories would work out-of-box for subdirectory scoping.

They don't. I had to patch several additional things locally to get subagents and supporting systems working correctly:

- `session/index.ts`:  `Session.create` and `Session.fork` use `Instance.directory` instead of `Session.directory.get()` when creating child sessions, so all subagent sessions (Task tool) inherit the wrong working directory

- `tool/registry.ts`: plugin tool context still passes `ctx.directory` (Instance-scoped) instead of `Session.directory.get()`, so plugin tools receive stale directory info

- `session/instruction.ts`: `AGENTS.md` and custom instruction resolution searches from the Instance directory, not the session's

- `format/formatter.ts` and `format/index.ts`: formatter config lookups and execution use Instance directory instead of session directory

Even with all of those patched, there are still gaps that require architectural changes and can't be solved at the session level:

- Right panel changed files (`file/index.ts`): the file tracking/diff system is InstanceState-scoped, so it always shows diffs against the repo root, not the worktree

- Right panel branch name: TUI header reads `Instance.worktree` and the main repo branch, ignoring the session's directory/branch

So the scope of this PR alone won't cover the full worktree experience I was hoping for.

That said, it's still relevant and valuable for basic single-repo layouts where you just need sessions to operate in a different directory.

Would love to see this rebased with at least the registry fix included, and ideally the subagent session creation fix (`Session.create` and `Session.fork` in `session/index.ts` using `Session.directory.get()` instead of `Instance.directory`. Without it any workflow that spawns child sessions via the Task tool will have those child sessions operating in the wrong directory).

Those two are one-liners that make a big difference for plugin workflows.

For the full OpenCode experience (changed files, path, branch, etc.) you can have the agents manage your worktrees, `cd` into the worktree path or sub-path, and spin up a separate instance.

### Result

Update: Regression persists in v1.3.6 (Linux Mint 22 / WebKitGTK)

I've upgraded to v1.3.6, but the core issues remain unresolved. Here is a technical breakdown of the current state on Linux:

Persistent Session Mismatch: >    * The Phenomenon: Sessions created via TUI/CLI are completely invisible in the Desktop GUI sidebar. Conversely, Desktop-created sessions are often not retrievable via opencode chat list in the same project directory.

Technical Clue: This seems to be a Directory Normalization/Hashing bug. On Linux, it appears the Desktop app and the CLI are generating different project_id or workspace_id hashes for the same absolute path (possibly related to trailing slashes or symlink resolution).

The "Flash-then-Blank" (GUI Death): >    * Even in v1.3.6, clicking a session in the sidebar occasionally causes the main chat area to flash the content for a millisecond before going completely blank.

Suspicion: This points to an uncaught exception in the Tauri IPC bridge or a WebKitGTK rendering deadlock. When the frontend React tree crashes due to a state-sync error, the entire view fails to recover.

Performance (N100/Linux): >    * The GUI performance is significantly lagging compared to the CLI. While the CLI is instantaneous, the Desktop app consumes excessive cycles just to render simple Markdown.

Environment Context:

OS: Linux Mint 22 (Ubuntu 24.04 based)

Kernel: 6.x

Webview: WebKitGTK (standard Tauri v2 environment)

CLI vs GUI: CLI works perfectly; GUI is effectively a "read-only/broken" experience right now.

Please investigate the persistence layer's path-matching logic on Linux. It feels like the "Source of Truth" is diverging between the TUI and the Desktop Electron/Tauri shell.

Update: Critical Session Indexing & Workspace Logic Failure (v1.3.6)

Despite the v1.3.6 update, the session management remains fundamentally broken on Linux. This is a core persistence/logic regression, not a UI glitch.

1. Cross-Directory Session Leakage:
Sessions are "bleeding" between unrelated projects. A session created in Project_A often appears in the list for Project_B, while being invisible in its original directory.

Analysis: The project_id / workspace_hash generation logic is failing to reliably distinguish absolute paths. This suggests a Path Normalization failure during the SQLite indexing phase.

2. Multi-Instance Desync (CLI vs GUI):
There is a severe "Source of Truth" conflict between the TUI/CLI and the Desktop GUI.

Symptom: Running opencode chat list in a terminal shows a different session history compared to the Desktop sidebar for the exact same directory.

Technical Clue: It appears the app is failing to handle concurrent database access or is using different caching strategies for the CLI and the GUI wrapper, leading to stale or orphaned metadata entries in opencode.db.

3. Empty List Paradox:
In many cases, the sidebar and CLI both return an empty list for a project that clearly has existing JSON session files in ~/.local/share/opencode/storage/sessions/. The indexer is losing track of physical files.

Request: Please prioritize a force-rebuild feature for the SQLite index and fix the Concurrent Write/Locking mechanism. The current session tracking is functionally non-deterministic.
